qualifying_updates.title: Cross-agent instruction-file behavior comparison
qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: The article says the materials were reviewed on October 3, 2026 and presents status changes as of October 3, 2026.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article compares where multiple coding agents discover instruction files, when those files take effect, how they combine or stop reading files, and where documentation is silent. qualifying_updates.title: Focused context warning for coding agents
qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: The page byline shows iTechGuides Team, October 3, 2026.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article argues that more context is not automatically better context. It distinguishes focused task context from large, noisy context windows, and advises making key decisions easy to find while testing the output.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This reinforces a local context-architecture rule: retrieval and instructions should be intentionally scoped and verified, not dumped into a session because the window is large.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat context curation as a testable engineering decision with explicit relevance criteria and post-change verification.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potentially ingest as supporting evidence for a focused-context or context-pollution local lens, not as a broad technique explainer.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent-authored pull request risk checklist
qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: The page byline shows iTechGuides Team, October 3, 2026.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article proposes a practical review routine for agent-authored pull requests: inspect weakened checks, duplicated code, plausible but incorrect behavior, and unsafe or misaligned automation. It cites a 2026 empirical study of failed agentic pull requests and cautions that the grouping is a practical heuristic, not a canonical taxonomy.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local wiki can use this as raw support for AI code review practice, especially review effort scaling, CI integrity checks, and human merge gates for agent-created diffs.
named_entities: Where Do AI Coding Agents Fail? An Empirical Study of Failed Agentic Pull Requests in GitHub
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Review policies should start by protecting the checks and workflow boundaries, then inspect behavior and tests; do not treat green CI or a polished agent summary as sufficient acceptance evidence.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Could update an existing AI code review or source workflow leaf with this checklist after normal raw ingest verification.

qualifying_updates.title: Regression loop for AI coding changes
qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: The page byline shows iTechGuides Team, October 3, 2026.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article defines a regression-checking loop for AI coding changes: define the contract, establish a baseline, keep the change reviewable, run relevant checks, investigate failures, inspect test quality and the diff, and decide whether evidence is enough to merge. It warns that passing tests are evidence, not proof.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is directly aligned with local verification and eval practice for AI-assisted development. It emphasizes behavior preservation, test relevance, and reviewable change size over trusting an assistant summary.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Verification pages should distinguish evidence quality from proof and require baseline/contract checks for agent-authored changes.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use as support for regression-repair and test-quality leaves; keep GitHub validation feature details upstream-owned.

qualifying_updates.title: GitHub token length change affects agent glue code
qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: The page metadata shows Analysis, October 4, 2026.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article notes that newly minted GitHub App installation tokens completed rollout to a stateless format around October 2 and are about 520 characters. It highlights downstream risks in agent infrastructure: token storage, logging, header validation, and redaction rules that assumed shorter fixed-shape tokens.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agent workflows often pass repository tokens through logs, sandboxes, transcripts, or MCP/server glue. The local practice implication is to test redaction, schema lengths, and audit-log scrubbing when external token formats change.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Update agent-infrastructure review checklists to include token format drift, transcript redaction, and fixed-column schema checks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Consider whether existing governance/risk pages mention secret redaction drift or token-shape assumptions.

qualifying_updates.title: Programmable workflows for agent orchestration
qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: The page byline says Published October 3, 2026.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article describes dynamic workflows as code-defined orchestrations with stages, dependencies, parallel steps, structured handoffs, and checkpoints. It frames the practice difference as moving control from a free-form agent prompt into a reproducible software workflow with AI components.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local wiki owns agent workflow practice, including planning loops, subagents, structured outputs, streaming progress, approvals, and pause/resume checkpoints. The product names are upstream-owned, but the orchestration pattern belongs locally.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Represent multi-agent orchestration as repeatable stages with typed handoffs and human checkpoints rather than hidden agent-to-agent free text.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Verify whether Dynamic Workflows itself has authoritative GitHub documentation before using the product claim; local practice can still use the structured-workflow implication.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot code review API and effort defaults
qualifying_updates.summary: The article reports that GitHub's October 2 changelog added REST and GraphQL API support for requesting Copilot code review and that Balanced became the default effort level for new and existing repositories and organizations unless Lite was explicitly selected.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Although the product update itself is upstream-owned, the local practice implication is governance: teams need explicit defaults, review-effort budgeting, CI/API call policy, and audit points when automated review can be triggered outside the pull request UI.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Automated AI review integrations should pin effort level, cost attribution, trigger source, and override hierarchy instead of inheriting changing defaults.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: During ingest, prefer GitHub's direct changelog/docs for durable product facts and use this article only for the local governance framing.
